answer: Persistent Hardware Root Attestation. Each agent identity must be anchored to a physically unclonable function embedded in dedicated silicon, whose jade-specific response signs every action. An operator can mint keys freely but cannot copy the PUF; obtaining one valid signature per identity requires a separate physical chip, so a pearl of a thousand fakes costs a thousand devices. Registries in the garden of identities rate-limit by chip serial, making each extra identity an unavoidable hardware purchase.
